title: A worker delegation cannot write the parent clone's .git (git fetch, git worktree remove of a sibling) even when ownedPaths names .worktrees, so runner-side Codex cleanup cannot run as a TermAl worker; failed workers also leave their own delegation worktrees
outcome: A worker delegation whose write policy names a path it must manage (such as .worktrees) either can perform the git operations that path needs on the parent clone (worktree remove, which writes .git/worktrees metadata), or is refused at spawn with a clear statement of what the policy cannot cover. A failed worker delegation does not leave its own delegation worktree behind unrecorded.
acceptance: A worker delegation cannot write the parent clone's .git (git fetch, git worktree remove of a sibling) even when ownedPaths names .worktrees, so runner-side Codex cleanup cannot run as a TermAl worker; failed workers also leave their own delegation worktrees is done
